entries.title: Psalms 32:8
segments: 8. Whether, as most likely, the language of David (compare

    I will ... mine eye--or, My eye shall be on thee, watching and directing thy way.

entries.title: Psalms 32:9
segments: 9. The latter clause, more literally, "in that they come not near thee"; that is, because they will not come, &c., unless forced by bit and bridle.

entries.title: Psalms 32:10
segments: 10. The sorrows of the impenitent contrasted with the peace and safety secured by God's mercy.

entries.title: Psalms 32:11
segments: 11. The righteous and upright, or those conforming to the divine teaching for securing the divine blessing, may well rejoice with shouting.
